title: SLO-classification-based timeouts, hedged requests, and idempotency contract
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We currently have inconsistent retry/timeouts/backoff behavior across internal services and public SDKs. This leads to surprising multi-region failover amplification, increased tail latency, and difficulty diagnosing production incidents. The goal of this ticket is to define a single, SLO-driven contract that standardizes: 1) request classification by SLO (latency/cost sensitivity), 2) client-side timeout and backoff families derived from those SLOs, 3) hedged request semantics for low-latency critical paths, 4) idempotency key shape and server semantics, and 5) circuit breaker and load-shedding interactions for runtime and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: A clear mapping from SLO class (critical/interactive/batch) to default client timeouts and maximum hedged attempts is documented.
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) implement the new backoff and hedging primitives behind feature flags with tests covering idempotency and duplicate suppression semantics.
Runtime honors idempotency key headers and exposes idempotency observability (accept/replay/dedup metrics).
Circuit breakers in the runtime and gateway expose consistent failure budgets and integrate with SLO class to determine short-circuit thresholds.
End-to-end playbook for rolling out, canarying, and rollback is published and validated in staging with synthetic load tests.
Dashboards show per-SLO-class latency, retry rate, hedged hit-rate, and deduplication percentage.
No visible elevated error-rate for customers in the canary cohort for 72h after rollout.
Security review completed for idempotency-key handling and replay protections (KMS/HSM where applicable).
proposal_summary: We introduce an SLO classification label on each RPC/HTTP route: 'critical' (P99 target < 100ms), 'interactive' (P99 < 1s), and 'batch' (best-effort). The SDKs will derive a conservative default timeout per class and a bounded hedging policy for 'critical' requests only. Hedged request policy: one primary call + at most one hedged retry after an adaptive delay (derived from moving percentile of tail latency). Backoff defaults: jittered exponential with class-specific base/backoff cap; e.g., critical: base=20ms cap=200ms, interactive: base=50ms cap=2s, batch: base=200ms cap=10s. Idempotency: a well-formed idempotency-key (uuidv4 + route fingerprint) is required for any non-read operation that may be retried/hedged. Servers must implement a deduplication window with strong-at-least-once semantics inside the window (accept/replay), and return 'Idempotency-Status' header with values {accepted, replayed, expired}. Circuit breakers: per-route and per-backend breaker computed from recent error rate and SLO burn rate; when tripped, the router should return a standard 503 with Retry-After and a structured 'failover-hint' for SDKs/policies to determine client-side actions (immediate failover vs. fast-fail). Load shedding: when runtime load > 85% of SLO-driven capacity, non-critical classes should be shed first using token bucket and priority queues. Observability: expose metrics and traces for attempts, hedges, idempotency dedup stats, circuit-breaker state transitions, and SLO burn rate.
detailed_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Why single hedged attempt? Multiple hedged attempts reduce tail but multiply load; bounded single hedged attempt strikes a balance for critical paths.
Adaptive hedging delay uses percentile tail (e.g., 95th) rather than fixed time to reduce unnecessary hedges under light tail; requires runtime percentiles to be available in near real-time.
Idempotency-key shape includes route fingerprint to reduce cross-route collisions but will be optional for legacy clients; SDKs will opt-in and surface helper helpers for generation.

Deduplication window default is 60s for most write operations; window length will be configurable per route and must be small enough to avoid unbounded storage but large enough to cover hedged retries and client retries.
Circuit breaker thresholds are tied to SLO burn rate to avoid premature tripping during short bursts vs. progressive tripping when sustained errors cause SLO violations.
Backwards compatibility: defaults live behind SDK feature flags and runtime admission gates; rollout will be gradual and telemetry-driven.
We avoid synchronous global coordination for hedging decisions to keep per-request path latency low; decisions are local to gateway/edge and SDK behavior.
sdk_changes: Add new RequestOptions.slo_class enum with values {critical, interactive, batch} and allow override per call.
Implement Hedger primitive: hedgedAttempt(max_hedges=1, adaptive_delay_source=runtime_percentile) and a PluggableBackoff interface so customers can override.
SDKs must include 'Idempotency-Key' header on eligible calls and surface Idempotency-Status from server response to client logs/telemetry.
Feature flag: 'slo-backoff-v2' to gate rollout across customers; instrumentation added to measure success before GA.
runtime_changes: Expose route metadata for SLO class in service descriptors and enforce conservative default timeouts at the gateway.
Record per-route latency percentiles in a near-real-time bucketed store for adaptive hedging decisions.
Implement idempotency store optimized for TTL-based deduplication (in-memory cache + durable backing for longer windows).
Add circuit-breaker controller that computes thresholds from rolling SLO burn-rate and propagates short-circuit signals to routers.
Introduce prioritized queues and token-bucket based shedding logic by SLO class.
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-SLO-class P50/P95/P99 latency, retry rate, hedged attempt rate, dedup accept/replay counts, breaker state counts, and SLO burn rate.

Alerts: SLO burn rate > 1.5 for 5m (pager), hedged attempt rate spike > 3x baseline for 1m (pager if also error-rate increased), dedup replay > 0.5% for critical paths (ops alert), sudden increase in circuit-breaker transitions (ops alert).
Tracing: attach 'slo_class', 'idempotency_key', 'hedged' tag to spans to enable root cause analysis across retries/hedges.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design): finalize contract and review with PM/Product Security/SDK owners (2w).
Phase 1 (runtime & SDK prototypes behind flags): implement toggles and basic metrics in staging; run synthetic tail-latency tests simulating cross-region degradation (3w).
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of traffic for selected customers; monitor hedged hit-rate, dedup rates, error rates for 72h (2w).
Phase 3 (wider rollout): lift to 50% then 100% with rollback gates if pager alerts fire or customer errors rise (2w).
Phase 4: post-rollout review, finalize documentation, and deprecate old backoff variants after 6 weeks.
test_plan: Unit tests for SDK helpers ensuring idempotency key generation and header emission.
Integration tests for runtime deduplication semantics (accept/replay/expired states).
Chaos tests that simulate region egress latency and ensure hedged attempt reduces P99 without causing >10% extra load in steady state.
Load tests to validate load shedding behaviour under 120% of capacity and verify non-critical classes are shed first.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Hedging increases load and may worsen outages if misconfigured. Mitigation: single hedged attempt, adaptive hedging, and initial canary cap at 5% traffic.
Risk: Idempotency deduplication storage growth. Mitigation: default short TTLs, route-level configurability, and batched eviction strategies.
Risk: SDK adoption lag causing mixed semantics. Mitigation: feature flags, opt-in beta, and backward compatible server behavior (treat missing idempotency as non-deduped).
Risk: Circuit-breaker oscillation under flapping conditions. Mitigation: hysteresis and progressive backoff on state transitions.
